Subject: Renewal pricing — urgent capacity reprofile

Hi Mina,

We’re kicking off our renewal discussion for BlueHarbor. Usage spiked more than anticipated in Q2 (attached summary) and we need to understand options to avoid significant overage exposure. Our current 12-month commit expires 2027-09-30.

Primary asks:
- Can we shift 40% of our annual commit from steady throughput to a short-term burst pool for the next 3 months?
- Would Redwood consider a temporary rate guard (price hold) for requests beyond committed units while we renegotiate?
- Are there credits or onboarding concessions available given the unexpected surge?

We’re hoping to finalize terms by early August. I can hop on a call if that helps.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Cloud Ops
BlueHarbor Systems
Attachments: BlueHarbor_Q2_usage_summary.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — urgent capacity reprofile

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear note and for sending the usage summary.

Short answer: yes, we can do a reprofile and a limited rate guard while you normalize. Proposed immediate approach:

1) Temporary capacity reprofile: reallocate up to 40% of your annual committed GPU-hours into a 3-month burst pool. That pool can be consumed above baseline without breaking the commit math.

2) 60-day rate guard: during the first 60 days of the new term, any overage beyond committed units will be billed at a capped rate (12% above current committed rate) instead of list price.

3) One-time operational credit: we can apply a one-off 10% credit against July invoices to offset the sudden surge (applied as a billing credit, not rebate).

4) Amendment timeline: we’ll draft a one-page amendment (attaching a first-pass) and include a DocuSign link for signatures. If you want a longer reprofile (e.g., 6 months) we can model the P&L and escalate to finance.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Ben for capacity numbers and Laura to confirm commercial sign-off. If that plan looks good I’ll send an updated amendment and a tracked DocuSign by Friday.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Jul 20, 2027 at 11:04 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear note and for sending the usage summary.

Quick capacity note from infra:
- We validated the Q2 spike: 210% week-over-week peak for inference tokens on inference-cluster-24.
- Reprofiling 40% of the commit into a short-lived burst pool is operationally feasible; we recommend soft-limits per day to avoid noisy neighbor risk.
- If BlueHarbor opts into the 3-month burst pool, we can reserve a guaranteed share and allow bursting beyond that to the extent spare capacity exists (best-effort).

Technical ask for BlueHarbor before amendment: provide target monthly peak hours and a preferred daily burst cap (example: 12 hours/day at peak instance profile). We’ll include that in the amendment.

-Ben

- Move the rate guard window to 90 days instead of 60 (gives us runway to finish load shaping).
- Replace the 10% one-time credit with a month-of-usage credit applied against the first invoice in the new term.

If Redwood agrees to those two items we can sign the amendment next week. Please send the final DocuSign link and the redlined amendment.
